correctness.rationale: The exact character-collision enumeration yields M4=18n^2-15n+4S with S the nonnegative sum of three pairwise row-correlation squares. The complex Fourier-row construction attains zero. Binary 4-type Walsh orthogonality yields S=4sum(c^2)-n^2 and uniquely balanced minimizing integer counts. Ternary squared character sums equal half the sum of three squared count differences, and a cyclic 3-column construction attains all three individual minima. Solving the uniform 3x3 count equations yields the cyclic optimizer matrices and factorial counts when 3 divides n. The all-n proof and finite exact checker are independent lines of supporting reasoning; finite enumeration alone would not prove the theorem.

value.rationale: The question is an exact, natural all-width phase-quantization problem for three-channel bilinear Fourier shells. The theorem identifies three different arithmetic phases: exact tightness at n divisible by alphabet period, unavoidable positive defects elsewhere, and infinitely recurring binary-versus-ternary preference reversals. It determines every optimizer via balanced discrete marginals, provides exact normalized binary optimizer counts for all widths and ternary counts for widths divisible by three, making the result more than a sample enumeration or a mere restatement of frame orthogonality.
